- When sentiment is high (≥0.7), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.4), model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 5% of spike magnitude.  
- Model consistently underestimates 3–5 day horizon; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for 3–5 day ahead.  
- If sentiment drops sharply after a peak, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 2–3 days.  
- Model shows mean reversion bias: if 10-day average is >80, forecast tends to overshoot; adjust downward by 1–2% if sentiment is neutral or declining.
